docs.title: Guard Core for EspoCRM
docs.text:
Guard Core for EspoCRM is an EspoCRM extension that adds application-layer security to the EspoCRM API. It is built on psr15-guard and the guard-core-php engine (both MIT).

It screens API requests for attacks, bans clients that misbehave, applies per-route policies and has a passive mode that logs what it would block without blocking anything. It is off until you enable it, and while off it adds one config lookup per request.

The extension registers one global API middleware (globalMiddlewareClassNameList), so it covers public/api/v1/ and the portal API. The guard runs inside the application, so it sees what a perimeter device cannot: the parsed JSON body, the route and the response status. It complements a reverse proxy or WAF, it does not replace one.

This extension holds no security logic. Detection, rate limiting, bans, headers and responses live in the engine. The extension reads the guard config, wires the engine to EspoCRM's logger and config, and registers the middleware.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• EspoCRM 9.0.0 or later.
  • PHP 8.2 or later.
  • Redis, optional, for rate limits, behavior rules and bans that hold across requests.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Installation: the zip, the upload and what uninstalling does.
  • Configuration: the guard keys, Redis, trusted proxies.
  • Usage and default policy: what you get with only guardEnabled set, and how to roll out from passive mode.
  • Telemetry agent: the optional agent.
  • What it covers and does not: the entry points and the known limits.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add the keys to data/config.php (or data/config-internal.php). They are not editable in the admin UI and are never sent to the front end.

'guardEnabled' => true,
'guard' => [
    'enableRedis' => true,
    'redisUrl' => 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379',
    'redisPrefix' => 'espocrm_guard:',
    'trustedProxies' => ['10.0.0.0/8'],
    'routes' => [
        'POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/' => ['rateLimit' => 5, 'rateLimitWindow' => 60],
    ],
],

Clear the cache after changing the config (php command.php clear-cache).

Settings you give override the defaults key by key. A route key is an optional method plus a path, and a null route entry switches a default route off. Every engine option is a key of guard (the named arguments of the engine's SecurityConfig), and every route option a key of a route (RouteConfig). An unknown key or an invalid route option throws instead of being ignored. Options that need a closure or an object (onBlock, authVerifier, customRequestCheck and similar) cannot be expressed in a config file and are rejected.

docs.title: Redis
docs.text: Redis is off by default. Without it, rate limits, behavior rules and bans keep their state per request, so under PHP-FPM they never trigger across requests. Set enableRedis and redisUrl. Only redis://host[:port] is supported: a URL with credentials, a database index or rediss is rejected, because the engine's Redis client connects by host and port only.

docs.title: Trusted proxies and ipAddressServerParam
docs.text: The guard identifies the client by REMOTE_ADDR. EspoCRM's ipAddressServerParam is not read. If you set it to something else (for example HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR), the guard logs a warning, and behind a proxy you must set guard.trustedProxies (and guard.trustedProxyDepth) so the client is resolved from the forwarded header. Without that every client behind the proxy looks like the proxy.

docs.title: Country filtering
docs.text: The optional ipinfo map (token, and optionally dbPath and maxAge) turns on the IPInfo country database for the engine's country rules.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: guard can hold a Redis URL and an agent API key. The extension declares both config keys at level system, so EspoCRM never returns them from GET /api/v1/Settings, for any user.

docs.title: What it covers and does not
What it covers
docs.text: The Slim API entry points: public/api/v1/ and the portal API, through the global middleware.

docs.title: What it does not cover
docs.text:
• Non-Slim entry points such as ?entryPoint=... URLs and the OAuth endpoints.
  • Default route keys are literal /api/v1/.... A subdirectory install or portal-specific routes need your own route keys.
  • A honeypot field on the public lead capture form needs a hidden input in the form view. The server side (honeypotFields on the route) works, the client part is not part of this extension.
  • Header exclusion from logs (logSensitiveHeaders) is not in the default policy: guard-core-php 4.4.0 throws a TypeError for a non-empty value. The engine still redacts Authorization, X-Api-Key, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie in its logs.
  • The guard is one layer. It does not replace a reverse proxy, a WAF or EspoCRM's own access control.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download guard-core-<version>.zip from the GitHub release, together with its .sha256 file, or build it (see below).
  2. Check the download with sha256sum -c guard-core-<version>.zip.sha256.
  3. In EspoCRM open Administration > Extensions, upload the zip and click Install.

From the command line the same install is php command.php extension --file=guard-core-<version>.zip, run in the EspoCRM root directory.

Installing changes nothing: guardEnabled is absent, so the middleware passes every request straight through. See Usage and default policy to turn it on.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Uninstalling removes the middleware and also deletes guardEnabled and guard from the config files. That is on purpose: the extension hides guard (it can hold a Redis URL and an agent API key) from the Settings API, and once it is gone nothing would hide those values from logged-in users. Keep a copy of your guard block if you plan to reinstall.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
npm ci
npm run extension      # builds build/guard-core-<version>.zip

The module bundles only rennf93/psr15-guard and rennf93/guard-core-php. The psr/* packages that psr15-guard requires are provided by EspoCRM itself, so the module composer.json replaces them and none ends up in the package. A size and content check runs in CI on every build.

docs.title: Telemetry agent
docs.text:
The guard-agent-php agent is optional and is not bundled. To use it, run in the EspoCRM root directory:

composer require rennf93/guard-agent-php

then add an agent map to guard:

'guard' => [
    'agent' => ['apiKey' => 'your-project-api-key'],
],

The extension loads the agent only when the package is present, and fails with a clear message when agent is configured without it. When an agent is configured, enableAgent defaults to true. The agent is started with the first guarded request and flushes its buffer when the request ends.

An EspoCRM upgrade replaces vendor/, so run the composer require command again after upgrading.

The agent API key lives in guard, which is hidden from the Settings API.

docs.title: Usage and default policy
docs.text:
With only guardEnabled set to true you get the default policy:

  • Passive mode: what would be blocked is logged, nothing is blocked.
  • Attack screening of paths, query strings, headers and JSON or form bodies is on.
  • No body scan on POST /api/v1/Attachment/chunk/.
  • A ban rule after more than 10 responses with status 401 in 5 minutes on GET /api/v1/App/user and on the API prefix.
  • Rate limits on POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/ (10 per minute) and on the two password routes (5 per 5 minutes).

docs.title: Rolling out
docs.text:
1. Set 'guardEnabled' => true and clear the cache.
  2. Watch data/logs for Guard would block by ... lines. Each line names the check, the reason and the client, and the request still passes.
  3. Fix or exclude what is a false positive, for example with a route policy.
  4. Set 'passiveMode' => false. Blocked requests now log Guard blocked by ... and get the engine's response (400 for a detected attack, 403 for a banned client, 429 for a rate limit).

Redis matters for steps 3 and 4: without it the rate limits and bans do not hold across requests.

docs.title: Route policies
docs.text:
'guard' => [
    'routes' => [
        // A stricter lead capture limit.
        'POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/' => ['rateLimit' => 3, 'rateLimitWindow' => 60],
        // Switch a default route off.
        'POST /api/v1/User/passwordChangeRequest' => null,
        // A ban after repeated 401 responses.
        'GET /api/v1/App/user' => ['behaviorRules' => [[
            'rule_type' => 'return_pattern',
            'pattern' => 'status:401',
            'threshold' => 3,
            'window' => 300,
            'action' => 'ban',
            'ban_duration' => 3600,
        ]]],
    ],
],

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: examples/simple_app runs a real EspoCRM with MariaDB and the default policy. examples/advanced_app adds Redis, an nginx reverse proxy with trustedProxies, passive mode off and the route policies above. Both install the built extension zip through EspoCRM's own extension install, and both are exercised by the Live Smoke workflow.
